what_breaks: Zoho is down or rejecting; no order placed in this window can be picked (picking is gated on zohoOrderCreationStatus=SALES_ORDER_CREATED)
runbook: Check Zoho reachability + token (look for ZOHO_TOKEN_401_REFRESH / GET_ZOHO_ACCESS_TOKEN_ERROR). Orders self-recover via the 30-min sweeper once Zoho is back - do not manually create SOs first.
notes: Known benign floor: the consumer retries once with test tax exemption on Zoho 110802, so a first-attempt error followed by success is normal. Correlate with ZOHO_SALES_ORDER_TAX_DIAGNOSTICS before escalating. Baseline before fixing the number.

what_breaks: Elevated Zoho rejection rate; a subset of orders is not getting a Sales Order
runbook: Sample 3 orderIds from the log, check the Zoho error body in meta.error_message. Usually item mapping or tax config on one SKU.
notes: Same 110802 caveat as the critical row.

flow: SO creation - backlog of orders with no SO
what_breaks: Orders are placed but no Sales Order exists, so they never enter the picking queue. Catches consumer death, queue death, and cron death in one signal.
runbook: Check the AmazonMQ consumer is alive and the ORDER_PLACED queue is draining. If the cron itself stopped, no datapoint arrives - alarm must be configured treatMissingData=breaching.
notes: This is the single most valuable alert in this flow - it is the business SLI, not a proxy. Non-zero floor is expected: H1/Rx orders awaiting doctor review legitimately sit pending. Baseline 2 weeks before setting the number. metricValue = $.meta.pendingOrdersCount

flow: SO creation - backlog of orders with no SO
what_breaks: Backlog building; SO creation is slower than order placement
runbook: Check whether the backlog is H1/Rx-pending (expected) or plain orders (not expected) via the fulfillment dashboard filter on zohoOrderCreationStatus.
notes: Split this into two metrics later - pending-awaiting-Rx vs pending-should-have-SO - the mixed number will always be noisy.

what_breaks: Stock check is failing across the board - likely Zoho stock reads returning zero or the reservation ledger is wrong. Orders get soft-blocked instead of picked.
runbook: Check a failing drugCode's location_available_for_sale_stock on Zoho directly vs mdm.item_procurement.stock_in_warehouse. A global spike means the Zoho read broke, not that stock ran out.
notes: Must be a ratio, not a count - INSUFFICIENT_QTY is a normal business outcome at low rate. Min-volume guard is mandatory or night traffic will page you.

what_breaks: Elevated soft-blocking; more orders than usual are waiting on procurement
runbook: Pull the top drugCodes from meta.drugCodeToZohoDetailsMappingObject and hand to procurement.
notes: Expect a real daily rhythm here. Baseline by hour-of-day before trusting one flat threshold.

flow: SO creation - failure handler itself failed
what_breaks: postSalesOrderCreationFailureActions threw, so the order was not marked SALES_ORDER_FAILED and no procurement reservation was written. The same stock can now be promised twice.
runbook: Pull meta.order.orderId for each. Verify zohoOrderCreationStatus and the matching order_item_procurement rows exist; write them manually if not.
notes: Rare but high blast radius - this is the one that corrupts the reservation ledger rather than just delaying an order.

flow: SO creation - failure handler itself failed
what_breaks: One order's SO-failure bookkeeping did not complete
runbook: Same check as critical, single order.
notes: Deliberately fires on a single occurrence - the cost of one missed reservation is higher than the cost of one Slack ping.

what_breaks: ORDER_PLACED messages are erroring past max retries and being nacked with requeue=false - the message is dropped and the order only recovers on the next 30-min sweep
runbook: Read meta.message for the failing eventData. If it is a systemic Zoho error, expect so-zoho-api-fail to be firing too - fix that first, this is downstream.
notes: Recoverable but delayed - dropped messages are re-enqueued by createZohoSalesOrdersViaCronV2 every 30 min. Escalate on the backlog alert, not this one, if orders are actually stuck.

what_breaks: Sales-order queue is erroring on some messages
runbook: Check whether the same orderId is looping - a poison message will retry to max then drop, and reappear via the sweeper every 30 min forever.
notes: Poison-message loop is the failure mode to watch for here: it looks like a low steady rate rather than a spike.

what_breaks: The AmazonMQ connection is down, so no ORDER_PLACED message is consumed at all. Every order placed from now on has no Sales Order.
runbook: Check broker health and the consumer pod. Restart the worker if reconnect is not happening. Orders placed during the outage recover via the 30-min sweeper.
notes: Fastest detector of total SO stoppage (minutes) - the backlog alert catches the same thing but takes up to an hour. Pair with AMAZON_MQ_RECONNECTED to auto-resolve.

what_breaks: Broker connection is flapping
runbook: Normal on deploy. Only investigate if it fires outside a deploy window.
notes: Will fire on every rollout - either add a deploy-window suppression or accept it as informational.

what_breaks: A handler threw something its own try/catch did not cover. Client gets a 500. THIS IS THE 'junior dev broke an API' CASE AND THERE IS CURRENTLY NO SIGNAL FOR IT.
cloudwatch_filter_pattern: n/a - cannot be built until the filter logs
runbook: BLOCKER: uncomment/restore the logError call in src/common/middleware/exception-filter.ts. Until then this failure mode is invisible.
notes: The global APP_FILTER catches every uncaught Error, returns 500, and emits ZERO log lines - the logging call is commented out. Fix the filter first; every row below is a partial substitute for this one.

what_breaks: Same as above at lower volume
runbook: Same blocker.
notes: Also fix while you are in there: QueryFailedError is returned as HTTP 400 with the raw DB message. A broken query therefore looks like a client error in any HTTP-level metric, and leaks schema detail to the caller.

flow: Caught server errors across all routes
what_breaks: Server-side failures are spiking somewhere in the app - broad breakage, likely a bad deploy
runbook: Group by $.meta.path in Logs Insights to find which route. Check the last deploy time first - this alert exists to catch bad releases.
notes: APP-WIDE = CATASTROPHE DETECTOR ONLY. With 837 routes across 72 controllers, one route going 100%-broken moves the global rate ~1 point and hides under any sane threshold. Per-route alarms (the ord-* rows) are what catch a single broken API. Also only covers errors a handler CAUGHT and logged - uncaught ones are invisible until plat-unhandled-5xx is unblocked.

flow: Caught server errors across all routes
what_breaks: Elevated server errors app-wide
runbook: Same triage. Usually one route dominates.
notes: Baseline per hour-of-day - a flat threshold will be wrong at both 3am and 8pm.

what_breaks: A deploy broke request validation, auth, or a contract the app/web relies on - clients that worked yesterday are now being rejected
runbook: Group by $.meta.path and $.meta.error_message. A single new message dominating = a contract change. Roll back before debugging.
notes: Same app-wide dilution caveat as plat-5xx. Two more traps: (1) QueryFailedError surfaces here as a 400 even though it is a server bug; (2) the global pipe is whitelist:false, so unknown fields are stripped silently rather than 400ing - some validation breakage will NOT show up as 4xx at all.

what_breaks: Elevated client errors - possibly one broken client version
runbook: Check whether it is concentrated on one app version or one route.
notes: 4xx has a large legitimate baseline (expired OTPs, invalid coupons, unserviceable pincodes). Ratio against total request volume, never an absolute count.

what_breaks: An unhandled rejection or uncaught exception at the process level - the pod may be about to die or is already in a bad state
runbook: Read the stack in $.meta.error_stack. Correlate with pod restart count.
notes: Fires on a single occurrence deliberately - these are always bugs, never load. Emitted by src/common/error-handler/global-error-handler.ts.

what_breaks: Customers cannot place orders. Direct revenue loss, and the most likely blast radius of a bad orders deploy.
runbook: Check the last deploy. Sample $.meta.error_message. If it is FAILED_TO_ACQUIRE_LOCK_INITIATE_ORDER, Redis is the problem, not orders.
notes: $.meta.path is req.url (raw, with query string), so parameterized routes need a trailing wildcard. Verify the exact string with Test Pattern - do not assume the Nest route template.

what_breaks: A minority of order placements are failing
runbook: Look for a single repeating error_message - usually one cart shape or one coupon.
notes: Known legitimate failures live here too: ORDER_FAILED_NO_ACTIVE_CART, ORDER_FAILED_COUPON_EXPIRE, DUPLICATE_ORDER. Exclude those TraceCodes or the floor will be high.

what_breaks: Orders stopped being created. Catches the failure the error-rate alerts CANNOT see: an API that returns 200 and silently does nothing.
runbook: Confirm against Metabase before acting. If real, check the last deploy and whether initiateOrder is returning 200s with no INSERT.
notes: The most important alert in this module and the one most teams never build. An error-rate alarm reads 0% when the endpoint 200s its way through a no-op. Must be a same-hour-of-day comparison, not a flat number - order volume has a strong daily curve. Set treatMissingData=breaching.

what_breaks: Order volume meaningfully below normal for this hour
runbook: Check for a marketing/app-release explanation before treating as an incident.
notes: Will false-positive on holidays and campaign gaps. Accept that, or exclude known dates.

what_breaks: Prepaid orders are not being created after successful payment. Customer has paid and has no order.
runbook: Check whether the order exists for the cartId. bulkVerifyStatus is the recovery path for callbacks that never landed.
notes: Highest customer-anger failure in the whole system - money taken, no order. Deeper payment-side coverage comes in the paymentsv2 pass; this row covers the order-creation half only.

what_breaks: Some payment callbacks are erroring
runbook: Cross-check the order was still created - the mutex + existingOrder branch makes most retries benign.
notes: Callbacks retry by design, so a single error followed by success is normal. Alert on distinct cartIds, not raw count, if the floor is noisy.

what_breaks: Orders are stuck at their current status - no shipment booking, no invoice, no picking progression
runbook: Identify which transition. QC_COMPLETED(61) failures mean no forward shipment is being booked - see modules/orders/status-machine.
notes: POST_ORDER_STATUS_UPDATE_ACTIONS_ERROR is the more dangerous of the two: the status moved but the side effects (shipment, invoice) did not.

what_breaks: Some status transitions are failing
runbook: Check for one order looping.
notes: IGNORED_STATUS_TRANSITION_RULE is a separate, expected code - do not fold it in.

what_breaks: Ops/CC cannot edit orders - blocks substitutions and salt changes, and a half-applied edit can leave cart and order out of sync
runbook: Confirm the edited cart and the order amount agree for a sample order before letting ops retry.
notes: Edit touches money (refund/top-up). A spike here is a Stop-and-Confirm-category regression.

what_breaks: Order edits are erroring at low rate
runbook: Most are status-gate rejections (order too far along). Check error_message before escalating.
notes: Legitimate floor from ORDERS_WITH_STATUS_ID_CAN_NOT_BE_EDITED and NEW_SALT_NOT_ALLOWED_AFTER_PICKER_ASSIGNED.

what_breaks: Customers cannot see their orders. High support volume, looks like the app is down even when fulfilment is fine.
runbook: Check the last deploy. Read paths break on null-deref far more often than write paths given strictNullChecks is off.
notes: Read-path breakage is the most common junior-dev regression and the least likely to be caught by a fulfilment-side alert.

what_breaks: Order detail reads failing for a subset of orders
runbook: Sample orderIds - usually one data shape (missing shipment, null patient details).
notes: Often a specific order state rather than a global break. Capture the orderId in triage.

what_breaks: Order placement is slow enough that customers abandon or the client times out
runbook: Check $.meta.url to see which downstream is slow, and $.meta.durationMs. Then check DB_SLOW_QUERY for the same window.
notes: REST_SLOW_CALL threshold is 3000ms by default (RestServiceUtils.DEFAULT_SLOW_CALL_THRESHOLD_MS), per-call overridable. DB_SLOW_QUERY is 10% SAMPLED (db-query-logger.service.ts:19) so multiply its count by ~10 before reasoning about volume. There is no true request-latency metric in logs - INITIATE_ORDER_STEP_TIMING is declared but never emitted.

what_breaks: Elevated downstream latency on order paths
runbook: Usually Zoho or ClickPost. Correlate before blaming our code.
notes: Prefer real p95 from the load balancer once confirmed available - see README. This log-based version is a stopgap.

what_breaks: Queries are failing. Depending on the call site this surfaces as a 500, or as a 400 with the raw PG message, or silently swallowed by a catch.
runbook: Check RDS status and DatabaseConnections first. $.meta.query identifies whether it is one bad query (a deploy) or all of them (the DB).
notes: BEST INFRA SIGNAL AVAILABLE - emitted by CustomTypeOrmLogger.logQueryError for EVERY failed query, unsampled, and the logger is wired into the datasource (db/data-source.ts:37). Unlike HTTP 5xx, DB failures are genuinely visible.

what_breaks: Some queries failing - usually one bad query shipped in a deploy
runbook: Group by $.meta.query. One repeated query = a code bug, spread across many = infrastructure.
notes: A single new query dominating right after a deploy is the signature of the regression class we care about.

what_breaks: Connection pool exhausted or RDS saturated - requests queue and time out before reaching the DB
runbook: Check which deployment is holding connections. Pool is max:30 min:5 per process (db/data-source.ts:19-27) times replicas times 5 deployments - budget it against RDS max_connections.
notes: No code needed - native metric, no log-shape caveats. connectionTimeoutMillis is 5000, so exhaustion shows up as timeouts not refusals. Also worth: FreeableMemory, ReadLatency/WriteLatency, DiskQueueDepth.

what_breaks: Connection or CPU headroom shrinking
runbook: Capacity-plan rather than firefight. Check whether a new consumer or replica count pushed it up.
notes: Replica datasource is separate - make sure read traffic is actually on it before adding writer capacity.

what_breaks: EVERY IDEMPOTENCY GUARD IS SILENTLY DISABLED. RedisMutex.acquire() returns true when Redis errors (mutex.ts:105-108, 'If Redis is down, avoid blocking operations'), so duplicate order placement, duplicate Sales Orders and double refunds all become possible while the app looks healthy.
runbook: Treat as a data-integrity incident, not a caching incident. After recovery, check for duplicate orders per userCartId and duplicate Zoho SOs in the outage window.
notes: The fail-open behaviour is deliberate (availability over consistency) but it means a Redis blip can produce duplicate money movement with no error anywhere. Pair with ElastiCache native metrics: CurrConnections, CPUUtilization, Evictions, DatabaseMemoryUsagePercentage.

what_breaks: Redis connection is unstable
runbook: Check ElastiCache metrics before assuming it is the app.
notes: Two independent ioredis singletons exist (CachingService and RedisMutex) - one can be unhealthy while the other is fine. See cross-cutting/caching in the wiki.

flow: Readiness probe failing - pods pulled from service
what_breaks: Pods are failing /pdp/health and being removed from the Service. If Redis is the cause this hits ALL pods at once because Redis is shared - a Redis blip becomes a full outage even though the app degrades gracefully otherwise.
runbook: Hit /pdp/health directly - it returns healthStatus{dbHealth,redisHealth} so it tells you which dependency failed. Do not restart pods; liveness is separate and correctly does not check dependencies.
notes: TWO PROBLEMS. (1) A FAILING READINESS CHECK LOGS NOTHING - checkHealth throws InternalServerErrorException which the global filter returns without logging, and SYSTEM_UNHEALTHY is declared in the enum but never emitted. This alert must come from k8s/Container Insights, not from logs. (2) Readiness gates on Redis (pdp.service.ts:436-452), so Redis down = every pod unready = total outage. Consider degrading Redis to a warning field rather than a readiness failure.

flow: Readiness probe failing - pods pulled from service
what_breaks: A subset of pods is flapping ready/unready
runbook: Usually one pod with a bad connection rather than a shared dependency.
notes: Expected during rollouts - suppress in the deploy window.

what_breaks: Containers are restarting - in-flight requests dropped, queue consumers repeatedly losing their connection
threshold: >= 3 restarts in 15 min for any deployment
runbook: Check for OOMKilled vs crash. Correlate with UNHANDLED_ERROR / UNHANDLED_REJECTIONS in logs and with the last deploy.
notes: SIGTERM_RECEIVED (main.ts:89) and SYSTEM_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN mark intentional shutdown - use them to distinguish a rollout from a crash. Worker deployments matter as much as the API here.

what_breaks: Occasional pod restarts
runbook: Check memory trend before dismissing - a slow leak shows up here first.
notes: Memory leaks in this codebase have a precedent (the shared https.Agent in RestServiceUtils exists to fix an SSL leak).

what_breaks: Messages are piling up with nobody processing them. Faster and more direct than any log-derived backlog signal.
threshold: ConsumerCount = 0, or oldest message age > 15 min
runbook: ConsumerCount=0 means the worker pod is down or never subscribed - check ENABLE_*_QUEUE_CONSUMER on the ConfigMap for that deployment.
notes: Strictly better than so-backlog-crit for detection speed (minutes vs up to an hour) - keep both, they fail differently. Also add DLQ depth > 0 for every SQS queue that has one; the AmazonMQ sales-order path has NO DLQ (nack requeue=false drops the message).

what_breaks: Queue depth or message age climbing
runbook: Check whether the consumer is slow or the producer spiked.
notes: RabbitMQ consumer runs prefetch(1) = strictly sequential, so a slow message head-of-line-blocks everything behind it. Depth climbing with ConsumerCount>0 usually means one slow message, not capacity.
